stem: A 64-year-old woman has had headaches for 25 years and takes several tablets of one of her medications every day. She now has flank pain and passes blood in her urine. Blood pressure is 158/96 mm Hg, creatinine is 2.4 mg/dL, and urinalysis shows sterile pyuria. CT shows small kidneys with sloughed tissue in the renal pelvis. She also takes digoxin, nifedipine, propranolol and warfarin.
oneliner: 64F + 25 y headaches + several tablets of one drug daily + hematuria, flank pain + Cr 2.4 + sterile pyuria + small kidneys with sloughed papillae + also digoxin, nifedipine, propranolol, warfarin → which drug?
ask: Which drug most likely caused her kidney disease?

whyNot.A: **Cardiac glycoside**: toxicity gives arrhythmias and visual changes, not papillary necrosis
whyNot.B: **Dihydropyridine**: causes edema and flushing, not kidney damage
whyNot.C: **Beta-blocker**: bradycardia and bronchospasm, not kidney damage
whyNot.D: **Anticoagulant**: bleeding is the danger; does not cause papillary necrosis

why: **Years of high daily analgesic use + sterile pyuria + small kidneys + sloughed papillae** = analgesic nephropathy with papillary necrosis, caused by chronic **aspirin / NSAID** use.

drug.name: Aspirin (NSAIDs)
drug.how: Irreversibly acetylates COX-1 and COX-2, lowering prostaglandins and thromboxane
drug.use: Analgesia, antipyresis, antiplatelet therapy, Kawasaki disease
drug.watch: Gastric ulcers, tinnitus, analgesic nephropathy and papillary necrosis, Reye syndrome in children, respiratory alkalosis then anion gap acidosis in overdose
